title: Closer

lines.text: You press play in Mumbai. The video lives on a server in Virginia.
lines.spoken: You press play in Mumbai. The video lives on a server in Virginia.
lines.hero: globe: a glowing dot in Mumbai, a dot in Virginia, an arc drawing across the ocean

lines.text: That is almost thirteen thousand kilometres away.
lines.spoken: That is almost thirteen thousand kilometres away.
lines.hero: the arc stretches; a distance counter rolls up

lines.text: Even at the speed of light in fibre, the round trip takes over a tenth of a second.
lines.spoken: Even at the speed of light in fibre, the round trip takes over a tenth of a second.
lines.hero: a light pulse runs out along the arc and back; a stopwatch counts

lines.text: Amazon CloudFront exists to shorten that trip.
lines.spoken: Amazon CloudFront exists to shorten that trip.
lines.hero: the arc snaps short; the title lands

lines.text: The idea is simple. Do not make the file travel. Put a copy near the viewer.
lines.spoken: The idea is simple. Do not make the file travel. Put a copy near the viewer.
lines.hero: one file icon in Virginia splits into copies that fly out to cities

lines.text: In two thousand eight, CloudFront launched with fourteen of these locations.
lines.spoken: In two thousand eight, CloudFront launched with fourteen of these locations.
lines.hero: fourteen glowing dots on the globe (8 US, 4 Europe, 2 Asia); counter

lines.text: Today there are more than six hundred points of presence, in over a hundred cities.
lines.spoken: Today there are more than six hundred points of presence, in over a hundred cities.
lines.hero: the globe floods with dots; counter rolls up

lines.text: Here is the journey of one request. Your phone asks DNS where the file lives.
lines.spoken: Here is the journey of one request. Your phone asks DNS where the file lives.
lines.hero: phone illustration; a DNS lookup card slides in beside it

lines.text: DNS answers with a nearby edge location, the one that should be fastest for you.
lines.spoken: DNS answers with a nearby edge location, the one that should be fastest for you.
lines.hero: the phone's request lights up the nearest edge among several; the others dim

lines.text: The edge checks its cache. If the file is there, that is a hit, and you are done.
lines.spoken: The edge checks its cache. If the file is there, that is a hit, and you are done.
lines.hero: edge rack with shelves; the file is on a shelf; green stamp; file flies back to phone

lines.text: If it is not, that is a miss. The edge asks a regional edge cache, a bigger shelf one layer up.
lines.spoken: If it is not, that is a miss. The edge asks a regional edge cache, a bigger shelf one layer up.
lines.hero: empty shelf; red stamp; request climbs to a larger regional cache

lines.text: Still nothing? Only then does the request travel all the way to the origin.
lines.spoken: Still nothing? Only then does the request travel all the way to the origin.
lines.hero: the long arc to Virginia lights up; the origin server glows

lines.text: The origin sends the file back, and every layer on the way keeps a copy.
lines.spoken: The origin sends the file back, and every layer on the way keeps a copy.
lines.hero: the file travels back; copies drop onto the regional and edge shelves

lines.text: The next viewer in Mumbai gets a hit.
lines.spoken: The next viewer in Mumbai gets a hit.
lines.hero: a second phone asks; the file flies from the nearby shelf almost instantly

lines.text: And if a thousand people ask at once, CloudFront merges them into a single request to the origin.
lines.spoken: And if a thousand people ask at once, CloudFront merges them into a single request to the origin.
lines.hero: a crowd of request dots funnel into one line to the origin

lines.text: Each copy stays fresh for a set time. When it expires, the edge checks again.
lines.spoken: Each copy stays fresh for a set time. When it expires, the edge checks again.
lines.hero: a countdown ring on the shelf copy; it empties, then refills

lines.text: The origin works less. The viewer waits less.
lines.spoken: The origin works less. The viewer waits less.
lines.hero: two bars shrink side by side

lines.text: The video was never really in Virginia. It was already next door.
lines.spoken: The video was never really in Virginia. It was already next door.
lines.hero: pull back over the whole globe: the long arc fades, the short arc stays bright

fact_notes: Mumbai to Ashburn, Virginia great-circle distance is about 12,855 km (computed from coordinates 19.08N 72.88E and 39.04N 77.49W). Ashburn is used as a representative Virginia location; a real origin could be anywhere.
Light in optical fibre travels at about 200,000 km/s, so 12,855 km is about 64 ms one way and about 129 ms round trip at the very least (physics, before routing and processing).

CloudFront launched in November 2008 with 14 edge locations: 8 in the US, 4 in Europe, 2 in Asia (AWS Networking & Content Delivery blog, '98, 99, 100 CloudFront Points of Presence', and the 15th anniversary post).

AWS describes the network as more than 600 points of presence and 13 regional edge caches in more than 100 cities across 50 countries (AWS blog). Wikipedia cites a higher number (1600+, May 2025), which conflicts, so the film says 'more than six hundred'.
Request routing: DNS routes the request to the point of presence that can best serve it, typically the nearest edge by latency (AWS CloudFront Developer Guide, 'How CloudFront delivers content').

Cache hierarchy: edge checks its cache, on a miss goes to the regional edge cache, then to the origin; the object is cached at the regional edge cache and the edge on the way back (same Developer Guide page).
Request collapsing: simultaneous viewer requests for the same file at an edge are collapsed into a single request to the origin (same Developer Guide page).

Caveat left out of the film for brevity: dynamic requests and PUT/POST/PATCH/OPTIONS/DELETE methods skip the regional edge cache and go straight to the origin. Cache lifetime is controlled by TTL settings and cache-control headers.
'Regional edge caches' were announced at re:Invent 2016 (AWS blog); not part of the 2008 launch, which the film does not claim.
